newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI eases rules for non-bank finance cos.
newsitem.headline: India RBI eases rules for non-bank finance cos.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Thursday it had exempted insurance, stock exchange and stock broking companies, mutual benefit financial companies (nidhis) and chit fund companies from some provisions of the RBI Act, 1934 as amended by the Reserve bank of India (Amendment) Ordinance, 1997.
The Ordinance was promulgated by the Indian government on January 9, 1997.

"As per the Reserve Bank's announcement, insurance, stock exchange and stock broking companies have been exempted from the provisions relating to the requirements of minimum net owned funds, compulsory registration with the RBI, maintenance of minimum liquid assets and compulsory transfer of at least 20 percent of profit to reserve fund," the RBI said in a statement.
It said these companies had been exempted as they are already regulated by separate regulatory authorities.
The RBI also announced changes in the regulations governing mutual benefit financial companies (nidhi companies) and chit fund companies.

"Nidhi companies, which are notified under Section 620A of the Companies Act, 1956 and the chit fund companies which are conducting chit business are not required to compulsorily register themselves with the Reserve Bank," it said.

"The stipulations of minimum net owned funds of 500 million rupees, maintenance of assets in government securities/guaranteed bonds and compulsory transfer of profit to reserve fund are not applicable to these companies," it said.

They would however continue to be regulated by the provisions of the directions issued to them by the RBI, other relevant provisions of Chapter IIIB of the RBI Act, 1934 and other Acts as applicable to them, it added.
Earlier, as per the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India (Amendment) Ordinance, 1997, the RBI had been empowered to regulate non-banking financial companies.
As per the Ordinance, all such companies were required to register with the RBI.

They had also been required to maintain minimum net owned funds of 500 million rupees, maintain liquid assets in the form of government securities/guaranteed bonds and transfer at least 20 percent of their profits to a reserve fund.
Non-banking finance companies as defined by the RBI Act include insurance companies, stock broking companies, corporate stock exchanges, nidhi and chit fund companies.
